name: Set and recover your own password on an account the system generated, so nobody else ever knows it
priorityReason: Every account in the system is generated by it, and no other route creates a credential.

goal.capability: to receive an account, set my own password and recover it if I forget
goal.outcome: only I ever know my password, and nobody had to create my account by hand

secondaryActors.involvement: Configures the password policy. Does not create credentials, does not issue them, and does not handle passwords at all.

externalActors.involvement: Delivers the temporary password and the one-time recovery code.

additional.description: An admission is completed, which generates the student's and the guardian's accounts (BR-1).

preconditions.condition: A record exists that the account is generated from — a completed admission or a created staff record (BR-1).
A contact is recorded against that record, since the temporary password is sent to it (BR-2).
The Super Admin has configured the password policy (BR-4).

postConditions: The account was generated automatically by the system, and nobody created a credential by hand.
There is no screen anywhere in the system for creating a credential.
A temporary password was generated and sent to the person on the contact recorded against their record.
The user was forced to change it before anything else could be reached, so nobody else could sign in to that account.
The password they set met the policy the Super Admin configured.
Only the user knows their password. The Super Admin does not, and there is no route by which anybody could.
A forgotten password was recovered by a one-time code, not by anybody issuing a new one.
A person who left had their account disabled rather than deleted, so everything they did stays on the record.
Every account generation, password change and reset is on the audit trail.

businessRules.rule: Credentials are generated automatically by the system. A student's and their guardian's account is generated the moment the admission is completed, and an employee's account is generated the moment their staff record is created. Nobody creates a credential by hand, and there is no screen anywhere in the system for doing so.
Together with the account the system generates a temporary password and sends it to the person on the contact recorded against their record.

The user signs in with the temporary password and is redirected straight to a change-password screen. The system forces the change before anything else can be reached, so nobody else can sign in to that account.
The user sets their own password, meeting the policy the Super Admin has configured.
A user can change their password at any time from the system, entering the current one first.

A user who has forgotten their password asks for a reset and the system emails them a one-time code. Once the code is matched the user is taken to the change-password screen and sets a new password. Nobody issues a password to anybody.
Nobody else ever knows a user's password, the Super Admin included. There is no screen that displays one, no route that retrieves one, and no person who can set one on somebody's behalf.
When a person leaves, their account is disabled rather than deleted, so it can no longer be signed in to while everything they did stays on the record.
Every account generation, password change and reset is recorded in the audit trail.
A one-time code is spent once and expires. A code that still works after it has been used is a second password.
A disabled account cannot sign in, cannot recover a password and cannot receive a temporary one.

transitions.condition: The temporary password is sent to the contact on the record (BR-2).
They sign in with the temporary password and set their own (BR-3, BR-4).
They ask for a reset and a one-time code is sent (BR-6).
The code is matched and a new password is set (BR-6, BR-10).
The person leaves. The account is disabled, never deleted (BR-8).
The person returns, for instance on re-admission or re-employment.

alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused and the policy is stated, so the user knows what is required (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The user has forgotten their password
alternateFlows.behaviour: A one-time code is emailed. The Super Admin issues nothing (BR-6, BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The code has already been used
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. A code that still works after use is a second password (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The person returns to the school
alternateFlows.behaviour: The account is re-enabled rather than a new one generated, so their history stays attached (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: Somebody else has the temporary password
alternateFlows.behaviour: The forced change means the account is only usable once, by whoever signs in first, and the intended user recovers it if that was not them (BR-3, BR-6).

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
